name: Islamic Republic of Pakistan

population.note: asOf 2025: 255,219,554 (World Bank). Range allows for 2026 change.

supportPersonnel.note: Active 660,000 minus infantry P roles 280,000 = 380,000. Air Force (~70,000), Navy (~30,000 incl. marines), armour/artillery crews, logistics and staff.

commandQuality.note: Rubric 0.5: competent staff system and recent operations (May 2025, Afghan border strikes 2025-26), politically dominant high command.

cohesion.note: Rubric 0.75: long-service regiments with strong identity.

morale.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75: high motivation against India, strained by insurgency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan.

weapons.note: Anchor 9: guided MLRS (Fatah), cruise missiles, PL-15 AAMs; mass of older guns.

armor.note: Anchor 8-9: Al-Khalid/Haider and T-80UD composite armour; Type 59/69 and Al-Zarrar older.

ships.note: Anchor 9: Type 054A/P frigates, AIP Agosta-90B, Hangor; no nuclear boats.

fortification.note: Anchor 9: hardened air bases and ditch-cum-bund defences on the Indian border.

logistics.note: Anchor 8-9: rail and motor transport, limited airlift (C-130 16).

communications.note: Anchor 9: data links on JF-17/J-10, Chinese satellite links; integration partial.

isr.note: Anchor 9: Erieye/ZDK-03 AEW&C, MALE UAVs, limited satellites.

air.note: Anchor 9 (4th/4.5 generation J-10CE, F-16 Block 52); J-35 not yet delivered.

cyber.note: Anchor 9: state cyber units, less capable than India/China.

gdp.note: asOf 2025. World Bank NY.GDP.MKTP.PP.KD (constant 2021 int$) 1,433,632,238,850 x 0.8005 (US GDP deflator 2011/2021) = 1,147,622,607,200 2011 int$. Range +/-15% for PPP benchmark uncertainty and the relative-price drift the rebase ignores. https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/PAK/indicator/NY.GDP.MKTP.PP.KD?format=json

milSpendShare.note: SIPRI via World Bank: 2.91% of GDP in 2025. Factbook: 2.5% (2024), 3% (2023), 4% (2021). High allows for the ~20% budget rise after the May 2025 conflict.

industrialShare.note: asOf 2025: industry incl. construction 20.1% of GDP (World Bank).

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess. Wheat/rice producer, food-insecure population, rice exporter; 2022 floods showed fragility.

annualCohort.note: asOf 2025. Males reaching military age per year = male population 129,314,682 x share of males aged 15-19 10.827% (SP.POP.1519.MA.5Y) / 5 = 2,800,181. Male population from SP.POP.TOTL.MA.IN. Males only (conscript-pool convention); about double if women are counted. Range +/-10% for single-year cohort variation.

roadKm.note: asOf 2025: 264,175 km total, 185,463 km paved (mid), 2,567 km expressway (list as quoted).

railKm.note: asOf 2019: 7,791 route-km (World Bank). CIA Factbook 11,881 km (2021, incl. sidings) as high. Broad gauge 1,676 mm.

majorPorts.note: CIA Factbook 2024: 3 ports (0 large, 2 medium, 1 small): Karachi, Port Qasim, Gwadar. All on one coast within ~500 km.

merchantTonnage.note: Educated guess. Below the 1 million GT threshold of the merchant-capacity list; Factbook 2023 lists 60 ships (5 bulk, 9 tankers). (context page: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/factbook/factbook.json/master/south-asia/pk.json)

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess. Rail-fed mechanised corps in Punjab/Sindh; little expeditionary capacity.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. Horses, mules, donkeys, camels (not from FAO data); Army mule units for the LoC.

nuclearWarheads.note: FAS Status of World Nuclear Forces 2026: military stockpile 170. Range +/-10.

homeDefense.note: Rubric 1.2: fortified border canals and cities, population support; 1.3 in the north-west mountains.

notes: Modern snapshot, asOf 2025 World Bank data with a 2026 order of battle. Population convention: inside ne:PAK (World Bank), i.e. Pakistan-administered Kashmir as the World Bank counts it. Money in 2011 int$ via derived:ppp-rebase-2011. Pakistan fought a short conflict with India in May 2025 and border clashes with Taliban Afghanistan in October 2025 and February-March 2026 (PAF airstrikes on Kandahar, Bagram and Paktika per the PAF article); losses disputed and not modelled. Equipment counts from Wikipedia equipment/aircraft/vessel lists quoting IISS for many lines (grade B/C). ships_major = frigates only; drones = Group 2+. Infantry splits, missile launchers, air-defence batteries are educated guesses. Paramilitary 291,000 excluded.
